        <h3>Match Log: Year 36 Hallowtide Tag, Reno Hallowtide Hollow (the third consecutive Wolves win)</h3>
        <div class="meta">LMG broadcast transcript · the only sanctioned-event match in the League with a one-knight scoring rule and no projectile combat · the broadcast booth's coverage is, by Hallowtide tradition, in lower-mic register because the Hollow is, on the night of the Tag, "supposed to be quieter than other matches" — the LMG's standing Hallowtide-Tag coverage protocol</div>
        <p>00:00 — Match opens. The Reno Hallowtide Hollow under the Hallowtide overlay (bats overhead, pumpkins lining the perimeter, gravestones serving as cover, the Reno academy's medical wing on standby for the inevitable melee injuries). Twenty knights from twenty teams enter. By Hallowtide Tag rule, all twenty are eligible to be "It"; the role passes by melee strike (no projectiles permitted in this event); the tagger keeps the role; tagged knights are frozen for three seconds during which they take heavy bleed damage; the match ends when only one knight remains alive; ranking is by death order. Kor Wartooth (WLF Brawler, two-time defending Hallowtide Tag champion) enters as the bookmaker's favorite. The Pandas have entered every Tag and have never finished above tenth.</p>
        <p>00:14 — Wartooth, by long-standing personal practice, opens "It" within fourteen seconds of match start by tagging the nearest available knight (this year: a Frog Speedster, who is, by every Tag's pre-match read, always the nearest available knight at fourteen seconds in because the Frog Speedster always sprints toward the perimeter at match start and never, in five Tag matches, makes it more than twelve paces). The Frog Speedster is frozen for three seconds and takes bleed damage. The Frog Speedster, in three seconds, dies. Wartooth retains "It." The crowd cheers. The crowd has, in five Tag matches, learned that the Frog Speedster always dies first.</p>
        <p>02:18 — Wartooth, holding "It," begins her tactical pattern — the slow patrol of the Hollow's perimeter, drawing other knights into engagement geometry where she can choose her target. The Hollow's gravestones are, by Whittlestone's overlay design, arranged in a deliberate non-grid pattern that favors patient hunters over fast runners. Wartooth is the most patient hunter in the field. The League's Tag-eligible knights have, in five Tag matches, learned to fear her perimeter walks.</p>
        <p>06:14 — First non-Frog death. Wartooth tags an Owl Sniper (Sundip Hootington III, the late Sundip Jr.'s younger cousin, on his second Tag entry). The Owl is frozen, takes bleed damage, dies at 09:22. Wartooth retains "It." The crowd's volume, by the LMG audio engineer's reading, is the lowest of any Year 36 sanctioned match — the Hallowtide tradition explicitly asks the crowd to be quieter than usual on Tag night, and the crowd, by long-standing personal preference, complies.</p>
        <p>14:38 — Mid-match. Wartooth has tagged four knights in the past six minutes — three Speedsters and a Brawler. The field is now sixteen knights. Wartooth is alone in the perimeter quadrant. The remaining knights have, by general unspoken consensus, abandoned the perimeter and clustered in the central gravestone formation. The clustering is, by Wartooth's reading, "the predictable mid-match defense formation. they will, in approximately four minutes, run out of patience and charge me. they always do. they will run, in their own time, to me." Wartooth waits.</p>
        <p>21:14 — The cluster breaks. Three knights — a Tiger Brawler, a Bison Speedster, and a Quetzal Brawler — charge Wartooth simultaneously. Wartooth, by her own pre-match reading, has been preparing for exactly this charge for the past six minutes. She does not engage all three at once; she engages the Bison Speedster (the fastest of the three) first, ducks beneath the Tiger's swing on her way toward the Speedster, tags the Speedster, and uses the Speedster's three-second freeze as cover from which to engage the Tiger. The Tiger is downed. The Quetzal Brawler, watching this, retreats. Wartooth retains "It." The cluster, having lost two of its three charging members, regroups in the central formation. The crowd, by Hallowtide tradition, does not cheer; the crowd makes a small collective sound that the LMG broadcast booth has, in three years of Hallowtide coverage, transcribed only as "the Hollow's hum."</p>
        <p>34:42 — Final two knights. Wartooth and a Helena Hedgehog (Spineholt Quillstrike, no relation to Hester, on his third Tag entry — the Hedgehogs have, in three years of Tag entry, never finished higher than fourth). Spineholt has, in the previous thirty-four minutes, been the only knight in the field whom Wartooth has not approached. The Hedgehog tradition has, by every Tag's pre-match read, drilled its knights specifically against Wartooth — the Helena combat circuit's match archive has, by Threadspine's standing instruction, included Wartooth tape since Year 33. Spineholt has watched, by his own pre-match interview, "approximately fourteen hundred hours" of Wartooth tape over his pre-Tag training period.</p>
        <p>34:51 — Wartooth and Spineholt circle. The crowd is silent. The crowd has, by long-standing Hallowtide tradition, gone fully silent for the final-pair circling. The LMG broadcast booth, by Mort Quillsetter's standing-Hallowtide-Tag instruction, has muted both color and play-by-play; only Quillsetter's own voice, in the standard scheduled-silence register, remains on the open mic.</p>
        <p>36:14 — Spineholt commits. He breaks the circle and charges Wartooth. He has, by every analyst's post-match read, charged at the moment Wartooth's pre-attack rhythm would have triggered her own commitment by approximately two seconds. The premature charge, by Spineholt's reading of Wartooth's tape, is the right call. He has read Wartooth's tape correctly.</p>
        <p>36:16 — Wartooth, having watched Spineholt's premature charge land approximately two seconds early, has prepared a specific counter that she has, by her own pre-match commitment, drilled for exactly this moment. The counter is a low feint into a step-back, into a tag at the moment Spineholt's spike-armor releases at impact. The tag connects. Spineholt is frozen. Spineholt takes bleed damage. Spineholt dies at 36:21.</p>
        <p>36:22 — Wartooth wins the Year 36 Hallowtide Tag. Her third consecutive title. The crowd, by Hallowtide tradition, does not cheer. The crowd makes the Hollow's hum at full volume. Wartooth walks, by tradition, to the perimeter and exits without a victory speech. The trophy — a small carved pumpkin with a single notched mark for each of her three wins — is presented to her at the back of the venue, away from the broadcast.</p>
        <p>36:51 — Quillsetter, on the open mic, gives the standard Hallowtide-Tag closing line: <em>"the Tag is over. the Hollow has had its night. we will see you at next year's Tag. by long-standing Hallowtide tradition, the broadcast booth will not, in the post-match coverage, replay the final tag. the final tag belongs to the Hollow. good night."</em> The broadcast cuts to black. The Hollow's hum, by every spectator's account, continues for approximately ninety more seconds after the broadcast cuts.</p>
        <div class="signoff">— LMG broadcast transcript · Year 36 Hallowtide Tag · Reno Hallowtide Hollow · Kor Wartooth's third consecutive title · the broadcast booth's standing Hallowtide protocol prohibits replaying the final tag · the protocol has, in three Tag matches, been observed without exception</div>
      </article>

        <h3>Match Log: Year 36 R6, RVN vs WLF (Pittsburgh, Foundry-Quarter Pitch) — the morning the perch was occupied</h3>
        <div class="meta">LMG broadcast transcript · 9:08 game time · partial · the match the broadcast booth has, by general agreement, never re-aired uncut · the match was scheduled to begin at the Pittsburgh foundry-quarter at first light, dawn-plus-three-minutes, and ran on schedule until the harbor-side event at the morning's first hour</div>
        <p>00:00 — First-light bell. Both teams take spawn. The Foundry-Quarter Pitch is, by Caucus measurement, three hundred and twenty paces along the long axis, set within the Murder's home ruin-quarter. The harbor wall — and, by Year 36 mid-season completion, the Visiting Perch — is visible at the field's northeast corner from the Wolf bench, at a distance of approximately one hundred and forty paces.</p>
        <p>00:32 — Round 1 opens. Wolves' Skir Greylane (Halfmoon's nephew, second-season Brawler, the lead of a three-Wolf rotation) drives center. Ravens' Quorrik holds the Sniper position at the back ledge.</p>
        <p>02:14 — Quorrik makes a clean ninety-eight-pace shot through Skir Greylane's right shoulder pauldron. Skir falls, returns to the Wolf line in two rounds (he carries three lives at this stage of the season). Ravens lead 1-0 in round 1.</p>
        <p>04:08 — Round 1 closes. Ravens take it on a 4-3 round-resolution, Quorrik with two kills.</p>
        <p>05:03 — Round 2 opens. Wolves adopt their standard mid-match defensive shift. The Ravens' Healer rotates to the back ledge. The match settles into the standard pace the LMG broadcast booth has come to recognize as Pittsburgh-home pace — slow opening, sustained ranged exchanges, no Brawler commits before the third minute.</p>
        <p>06:48 — On the Wolf bench, the team's spotter (a corvid auxiliary the Wolves contract from the Murder's older retired-flier pool) signals to the Wolf coach. The signal is the spotter-flag the Murder uses for harbor-watch communications: a single short flag-raise, then a pause, then a second short raise. The Wolf coach watches it. The Wolf coach is the only non-Murder coach on the active sideline who reads the harbor flag-code; she has, by her own pre-season acknowledgment, learned it for occasions of this kind.</p>
        <p>06:52 — Halfmoon Greylane, watching from the Wolf dugout in her standing veteran's-bench role (she has not started a sanctioned match since Year 35 R12, her shoulder; she travels with the team), looks toward the harbor wall. Inkbeak Sr.'s harbor-watch silhouette is visible at the wall's standing reception position. Halfmoon nods once, slowly, in the way the Wolves nod for things they have been told to expect.</p>
        <p>07:11 — Quorrik takes a second shot on the Wolf line. The shot is a clean kill. Ravens score the round, take it 2-0.</p>
        <p>07:48 — Inkbeak Sr.'s silhouette at the harbor wall straightens, in the way a senior watcher straightens at the moment of a confirmed sighting at terminal-approach distance. The Wolf spotter raises the harbor flag a third time. The Wolf coach signals to the Wolf bench: <em>break-protocol, harbor</em>. The Wolves' active line, by Year-35 standing arrangement with the Murder, knows what the protocol means. The Wolves' active line stops engaging at the round's next reset.</p>
        <p>08:14 — Round 3 opens. The Wolves do not, on the bell, advance. The Ravens, watching the Wolf line hold position at spawn, also do not advance. The LMG broadcast booth, watching both lines hold, calls the situation: <em>"the harbor bell has rung. the Cóndor is on approach. the match has, by long-standing arrangement, ceded the working morning to the harbor's working morning. we are, on this morning, watching two things at once."</em> The booth cuts the broadcast to a wide-shot covering both the field and the harbor wall.</p>
        <p>08:46 — At the harbor wall, the Cóndor is visible at the watch's standing visibility distance — approximately fifteen kilometers, with the morning's lifting fog still partial. Inkbeak Sr.'s silhouette holds the standing reception position. The Roost, gathered along the wall in the wider reception formation, is visible to the broadcast camera as approximately three hundred Ravens, evenly spaced, motionless.</p>
        <p>09:01 — On the field, both teams stand at spawn. The Wolves' Healer (Pinedrift, the same Healer Halfmoon Greylane carried across forty-eight paces in Year 35) takes off her helmet at her own bench's quiet recommendation. The Ravens' Healer, watching her, also removes hers. The active lines do not move. The crowd is, by every account, silent.</p>
        <p>09:06 — At the harbor, the Cóndor touches the perch's small ledge. The four-second acknowledgment runs. Inkbeak Sr.'s silhouette completes the acknowledgment in the standing way. The Roost, in the wider formation, completes the acknowledgment in unison. The broadcast camera holds the wide shot.</p>
        <p>09:08 — On the field, the round resumes. The active lines re-engage at the standing pace. Quorrik, at the back ledge, takes the round's first shot at the Wolf Brawler. The shot is a clean kill. The Ravens close the round 3-0. The match ends in the round's final minutes with a Raven 5-3 round-resolution and a Raven 3-0 match-resolution.</p>
        <p>09:48 — Post-match line. The Wolf captain (a third-season Brawler named Stormrun Greylane, Halfmoon's daughter, in her first season as captain) approaches the Raven line for the standing handshake. Quorrik, who is the Raven captain, accepts the handshake. The two captains hold the handshake for the standing one-second duration. Halfmoon Greylane, from the Wolf dugout, walks the long way around the pitch toward the harbor wall. She does not, by every account, look at any other Wolf or any other Raven. She walks to the harbor wall. She stands at the wall, twenty paces from the Roost's reception formation, in the position the Murder uses for visiting non-Murder fliers when they wish to acknowledge a perch event without participating in the formation. She holds the position for eleven seconds. The duration is the same eleven seconds the Wolves use for the bow. The Roost, watching her, completes a four-second acknowledgment of her acknowledgment in unison. Halfmoon nods once. She walks back to the dugout. The match's final ceremony is, by Caucus archive, considered concluded at this nod.</p>
        <div class="signoff">— LMG broadcast transcript · Year 36 R6 RVN vs WLF · the broadcast has, by Roost vote and Wolf coaching staff agreement, never been re-aired uncut · the harbor-coverage segments are, by Roost preference, available to the Foundation Archive only on Roost-vote permission · Halfmoon Greylane's eleven-second acknowledgment at the harbor wall is, by Caucus archive classification, "do not edit" · the LMG has, in three subsequent broadcasts, never re-cut it · the Wolves' standing position on Halfmoon's gesture: <em>"the bow is for what the Wolves have lost. the harbor acknowledgment is for what the harbor has, on this morning, gained. the eleven seconds are the duration. the duration was set on the bow's first observation. the duration is, on this matter, the right duration for both."</em> Halfmoon has not, in any subsequent interview, commented on the gesture · the Roost has not, in any subsequent Roost minute, formally named it · the broadcast booth, on the morning of the match, called it only the harbor acknowledgment · the name has held</div>

      <article class="match-log">
        <h3>Year 32 R4 · KIT vs RCC, Reno Open Court · the Five-Finger Friendship</h3>
        <div class="meta">Match Log · Reno · Pawington Cup-format friendly · the only match on record where every starting weapon was scavenged at least twice before the final round</div>
        <p>The match opened with the standard ten-knight loadout. By round three's halfway mark, the original carriers of nine of the ten weapons had perma-died, returned, or been scavenged from. The single weapon that remained with its starting carrier was, by the broadcast booth's own count, Mira Pawington's Stun Baton — and only because Mira was, that night, dropping each of her own kills' weapons into a small pile on the centerline that the Raccoons collectively, by post-match interview, agreed they "were not, on the matter, brave enough to approach."</p>
        <p>Final score: KIT 3, RCC 2. The Pawington Cup's small bracket awarded the Kits the trophy. The Raccoons, in a gesture that cost three lobsters in Foundation paperwork, sent Mira a small dressed-leather pouch the following morning. The pouch contained nine pawn tickets, made out to the active Raccoon roster, for nine items the Raccoons had not, that night, been able to scavenge. The Kits' bench has, on the matter, kept the pouch. The pouch is, by Kits' tradition, opened once a year on Mira's birthday and the tickets are read aloud, then refolded.</p>
        <div class="signoff">— LMG broadcast archive · KIT vs RCC, Y32 R4, Reno Open Court</div>
      </article>

      <article class="match-log">
        <h3>Year 33 R7 · BVR vs OTR, Olympia Harbor Pitch · the Long Snatch's Last Run</h3>
        <div class="meta">Match Log · Olympia · the final formal Long Snatch before the format was retired</div>
        <p>The Otters' tradition was, on the matter, settled before the bell: the Long Snatch — the colored kerchief carried corner-to-corner under team escort — would run one last time before the formal Capture-the-Pole bracket replaced it the following season. The kerchief was Pawington's: black wool, eighteen inches square, embroidered with a small otter, retrieved for the occasion from the locker corridor where it has hung since her death.</p>
        <p>The carrier was Pellic Slipstream, then a fourth-season Otter Speedster, who had, by his own admission, never once in practice held the kerchief without dropping it. He carried it the full corner-to-corner distance, did not drop it, was tagged at the final pole by a Beaver Tank named Driftwood Bristlebeard (now retired), and handed the kerchief back to the Olympia bench in one motion as he was tagged. The Beavers won the round. The Otters won the match three rounds later. The kerchief returned to its hook the following morning. It has, in three seasons since, not been moved.</p>
        <p>Pellic does not, on the matter, talk about the run. He has, in the years since, become the Otters' senior coach. He keeps the locker corridor's hook in good repair. The Otters' bench, by tradition, do not, on the matter, ask him about the run either.</p>
        <div class="signoff">— LMG broadcast archive · BVR vs OTR, Y33 R7, Olympia Harbor Pitch</div>
      </article>

      <article class="match-log">
        <h3>Year 35 R2 · LYX vs PLR, Anchorage Frostfall Hall · the only Lynx home game</h3>
        <div class="meta">Match Log · Anchorage · the Lynx's first match in the League · the only one they have, on the matter, won</div>
        <p>The Lynx had, by their senior coach Tessik Snowstep's own admission, no plan beyond <em>"see what they do, then do the opposite."</em> The Polar Bears, on their home Frostfall floor, had eight seasons of advantage. The match opened in the slow rotation the Polar Bears had used to mid-bracket the Year 34 closeout, and the Lynx — five solitary knights who had, by team tradition, met as a group only that morning — did the opposite of slow rotation. They scattered. They did not group. They picked, by Tessik's later analysis, the worst possible engagement angle on each round individually, and won them all anyway.</p>
        <p>The Polar Bears, in the post-match Frostfall Hall lobby, were heard to say (in a phrase the Anchorage broadcast picked up in the background of an unrelated interview): <em>"the Lynx do not, on the matter, do anything we expected. The Lynx are, on the matter, terrible at being a team. The Lynx win when there is no team to coordinate against."</em> The Lynx have, in five subsequent matches against the Polar Bears, lost every one. The Lynx have, on the matter, kept this single win on the wall of the Yukon Boreal Council post office. The post office is, on the matter, twelve days' hike from the nearest Lynx training tree.</p>
        <div class="signoff">— LMG broadcast archive · LYX vs PLR, Y35 R2, Anchorage Frostfall Hall</div>
      </article>

      <article class="match-log">
        <h3>Year 34 R6 · WLF vs FRG, Fresno · the eleven-second pause that wasn't, in fact, the eleven-second pause</h3>
        <div class="meta">Match Log · Fresno · a procedural curiosity</div>
        <p>The Wolves' captain Halfmoon Greylane's eleven-second post-kill bow was, by every Wolves' bench-staff record, observed in this match — but only because the broadcast booth, due to a documented signal error in the Fresno feed, replayed the same eleven-second clip twice in succession during the post-round break. Greylane bowed once. The clip aired twice. The Wolves' team, watching the booth feed in their bench dressing-room, briefly believed Greylane had bowed for twenty-two seconds. They were, by their own subsequent admission, "concerned." The bench staff did not, on the matter, correct the team. The team did not, on the matter, ask. The bench staff has, on the matter, never spoken of it again.</p>
        <p>Greylane has not, in any season since, bowed for a duration other than eleven seconds. The Fresno feed has not, in any season since, doubled a clip. The Wolves' team has, on the matter, not asked their bench staff about the incident. The Wolves' bench staff has, on the matter, taken the silence as a small mercy.</p>
        <div class="signoff">— LMG broadcast archive · WLF vs FRG, Y34 R6, Fresno · with editor's note re. the doubled clip</div>
      </article>

      <article class="match-log">
        <h3>Year 35 R6 · WLF vs OWL, Brewer's Reach Pitch · the broadcast caught the Ewe</h3>
        <div class="meta">Match Log · Brewer's Reach · the only sanctioned match in eight seasons where a single fan's voice carried clearly through the booth feed for the duration of the post-match line</div>
        <p>The match itself was, by Foundation match summary, a 4-2 Owls win in seven rounds. The standout play was a Greylane carry that did not, in any review, become anyone's career highlight. The standout MOMENT was the post-match line — eleven seconds of Wolves' Bow, the Owls' bench standing in silence opposite, the Brewer's Reach crowd at the kind of quiet that only Brewer's Reach can do — and, audibly through the booth feed: <em>"GREYLANE!!! KEEP HOLDIN' THE LINE, KID!!! BY JINGO YOU'RE GLORIOUS!!!"</em></p>
        <p>The booth director, by archive note, did not cut the audio. The senior commentator did not address it on-mic. Estelle, by booth log, looked at the senior commentator and waited. The senior commentator waited back. Neither spoke. The eleven seconds completed in the Ewe's voice and the natural ambient of an otherwise-silent crowd.</p>
        <p>The post-match wrap, when it came, opened with the senior commentator's only direct on-mic acknowledgment of the Ewe in eight seasons: <em>"and that, ladies and gentlemen, was Section 14, exactly as Section 14 wanted to be heard. The booth, on the matter, declines to interpret further."</em> The clip is in the LMG broadcast archive under the file name <em>"Y35 R6 — Greylane bow — Section 14 audible — booth declined."</em></p>
        <div class="signoff">— LMG broadcast archive · WLF vs OWL, Y35 R6, Brewer's Reach Pitch</div>

      <article class="match-log">
        <h3>Year 33 R7 · BVR vs SHK, Brewer's Reach Pitch · the closeout match where the Ewe arrived</h3>
        <div class="meta">Match Log · Brewer's Reach · the Y33 closeout · the broadcast booth's earliest archived Pew-Pew Ewe ambient capture (the booth would not formally identify her until two seasons later)</div>
        <p>The match itself was a 5-3 Beavers win in seven rounds. The standout was a Bristlebeard-the-Second double-tap on the Sharks' Tank in the fifth round, which Bristlebeard would later cite, in his own quiet way, as "the kill that bought my passage past the second-year shadow." The booth's call was clean, the crowd was loud, the Beavers were, on the matter, ahead.</p>
        <p>The detail of cultural-archive interest, by booth log: in the third round, on a Sharks Sniper draw at 240 paces, the booth's ambient feed picked up — clearly, against the Brewer's Reach crowd's general roar — the syllables: <em>"PEW! PEW!"</em> in a single voice. The booth director did not flag it. The senior commentator, by his own subsequent memo, "thought it was, on the matter, a child mimicking the laser-rifle audio effect." The senior commentator had, by his own admission, never visited Section 14 prior to Y35 R6.</p>
        <p>The booth's archival recording of the third round of this match is, by Foundation cultural-archive cross-reference, the earliest dated audio of the Pew-Pew Ewe's catchphrase. The Foundation has, on the matter, indexed the recording under <em>"Y33 R7, BVR vs SHK, Round 3, ambient — first Pew-Pew Ewe documented capture, retroactive identification."</em> The senior commentator's reaction to the retroactive identification, given to Stripewhisker in private at the Y35 closeout, was reported by Stripewhisker's own memo as: <em>"he laughed, on the matter, for what I would call a long time. Then he stopped. Then he said: 'I owe Section 14 a visit.' He has, on the matter, made that visit."</em></p>

        <h3>Year 30 R3 Tampa Flat-Batch — A Reconstruction</h3>
        <div class="meta">Match Log · Tampa Bay venue · the match the Caucus voted 11-4 to let stand · reconstructed in Y33 from Reef Tinkerbarrel's eighth Lobster Reach Daily installment + the Sharks' bench staff's annotated copy</div>
        <p>The Sharks-vs-Foxes match-of-record. The Sharks went 5-0 over the Foxes; the score is in the books. What was not in the books, until Reef Tinkerbarrel published the eighth installment of his Lobster Reach Daily memoir three seasons later, was the loadout-side note: the Sharks were, that match, running on Pell Whittlestone's flat-batch shipment from the Boise Foundry. The flat batch, by Whittlestone's own quiet acknowledgment in her Y33 Annual essay, "had a viscosity profile that did not, on the matter, match the spec sheet."</p>
        <p>The Sharks' Y30 captain knew. The Foxes did not. The match was, by Foundation reconstruction, decided in the round-two engagements: the Sharks' Tanks were, on the matter, two paces faster than they should have been, because the float gas in their armor was lighter than the Foxes' float gas by a margin small enough not to register on the pre-match weight check but large enough to matter in the third decisive turn. The Foxes lost the round. The Foxes then lost the next four. The Sharks went 5-0.</p>
        <p>The Caucus's Y33 vote (11-4 to let the result stand) was, by Caucus secretary's quiet note, "the only Caucus vote where the dissenters were also, on the matter, those most familiar with the technical details." The four dissenters were: the Foxes' Caucus delegate, the Beavers' Caucus delegate, Whittlestone (in her standing Caucus consulting seat), and the lobster vendor (in her standing Caucus consulting seat, which the Caucus established in Year 30 by a unanimous vote and which she has, in eight seasons, attended exactly twice). The eleven affirmatives were, by the secretary's note, "those who valued the integrity of the standings over the integrity of the loadout." The Sharks acknowledged the practice and apologized publicly. The Foxes accepted publicly. Reef Tinkerbarrel did not, on the matter, retract.</p>
        <div class="signoff">— LMG broadcast archive + Lobster Reach Daily · Y30 R3 SHK vs FRG, reconstructed Y33</div>

        <h3>Year 36 R2 · LYX vs ANT, Saint-Laurent Antlerstone Pitch · the Lynx's first away match</h3>
        <div class="meta">Match Log · Saint-Laurent · Estelle's first formal translation match · the only match in League history with a documented mid-match official-language switch</div>
        <p>The match was 4-1 Antlerlords. The standout was Marc-Olivier Brisefer's third-round single-handed Power Core defense (he held the Core for forty-eight seconds against three Lynx, two of whom would later credit him in their post-match scout reports as "the cleanest defensive line we have, on the matter, encountered all season").</p>
        <p>The cultural-archive detail: at 14:18 game time, the Antlerlords' bench-staff signal-caller switched the in-team communication language from League Common to Quebec creole — a switch the Antlerlords are, by team tradition, allowed to make at any point in any match without notification. The Lynx's senior coach Tessik Snowstep, listening to the bench feed via the visiting-team comms, did not, on the matter, immediately understand. Estelle, in the broadcast booth, did. Estelle quietly translated the Antlerlords' next three calls into League Common on the booth feed, where the Lynx's bench staff (who were, on the matter, listening to the broadcast as a backup) caught the translations and relayed them to Tessik.</p>
        <p>Tessik's own subsequent memo, by Foundation cultural-archive cross-reference: <em>"the booth has, on the matter, become a player. The booth's translator has, on the matter, become an asset. We will, on the matter, have to think about this. The booth is not, on the matter, supposed to be a player. The booth is, on the matter, becoming one anyway. The League will, in due course, address."</em> The Caucus has, on the matter, addressed: as of Y36 closeout, the booth's translator is, by formal Caucus ruling, "a neutral broadcast resource — translations are public to all parties and not subject to team-specific gating." Estelle has, on the matter, said only: <em>"this is, on the matter, what I have always done. The Caucus has, on the matter, simply caught up."</em></p>
