          <details class="lore-glossary-bucket" open>
            <summary><span class="bucket-letter">S</span> <span class="bucket-count">11 terms</span></summary>
            <dl class="lore-glossary-bucket-list">
              <dt>Sandbagged Knight</dt>
              <dd>A knight who is performing measurably below their stat sheet for reasons unrelated to injury, fatigue, or known field conditions. The most common cause, since Year 35, is the Personal Sandbag item. The term predates the item — it was originally used to describe knights whose teams had quietly arranged for them to lose, in order to extend the franchise's playoff window. The Commissioner's Office prefers the post-LY-8 usage and has discouraged the older sense.</dd>

              <dt>Sandshine's Threshold</dt>
              <dd>The Coyotes' standing rookie benchmark for la borradura — the disappearing — set at four-point-six seconds of sustained visual disappearance from a senior line during drift training. Named for Tachi Sandshine (CYT Speedster, Year 36 rookie season) who hit the threshold on her two hundred and thirty-eighth repetition during week six of pre-season training under Coach Reyna. The threshold pre-dates Sandshine — the Coyotes have used it since their pre-League regional combat circuit days — but the canonical name was attached to her record by Coach Reyna's standing tradition of naming the rookie threshold after the most recent rookie to clear it, "so the next rookie has a name to chase rather than a number." Sandshine's name will, by tradition, be replaced by the next rookie's at next pre-season. As of Year 36 mid-season the threshold remains hers; she has, in twelve sanctioned matches, cleared it against five different teams.</dd>

              <dt>Scavenging</dt>
              <dd>Picking up gear from a fallen Knight on the field. Scavenged gear retains its previous owner's name in the lineage chain (e.g., "Vela's Plate Cuirass"). Items with high scavenge counts become legendary; the most-scavenged item in League history is Bristlebeard's Riot Shield (7 carriers across 6 seasons).</dd>

              <dt>Sigridweave (Sgw)</dt>
              <dd>The senior curator of the Foundation Library Northeast Coast Bureau, an Owl who has held the curatorship since Year 31. Authoress of the canonical pencil-marginalia annotation style ("— sgw") that distinguishes the Bureau's working notes from the Library's official-ink filings. Sigridweave is, by every Foundation Library archivist's account, the most-respected working curator in the League — not for the volume of her output (the Northeast Coast Bureau is one of the smaller Foundation outposts) but for the quality of her judgment on the question of which sources to file at what level of confidence. The Old World File's six-year operating record is, by every internal Library review, principally her work. The Year-34 albatross of Old World File Entry 53 was, on the third afternoon of the visit, interviewed by Sigridweave in person; the bureau's standing protocol assigns long-stay visitors to the senior curator personally for the closing interview. Sigridweave's draft response to the albatross — <em>"To a Careful Narrator, from a Careful Library"</em> — was filed in the Foundation Drawer in Year 36 mid-season after two years of drafting; the draft remains, as of this filing, undispatched. Sigridweave's standing public position on the question of dispatch: <em>"the writing is what i owe the file. the dispatch, if it happens, will be what i owe her. these are different debts. they are, by my own preference, kept on separate ledgers."</em></dd>

              <dt>Slatequill Inkbeak Sr.</dt>
              <dd>The senior flying Raven of the Pittsburgh Murder, in his twenty-seventh flight year as of Year 36, who undertook the first sanctioned northbound-southbound oceanic flight in modern League history in Year 33. Inkbeak's eleven-day flight from Pittsburgh to Cartagena, his forty-one-day stay in Federación territory, and his seventeen-page handwritten communiqué are the canonical first-contact documentation between the two leagues. He has, in the four years since, made seven additional Caribbean-basin flights and continues to fly the route annually. Inkbeak is the only confirmed-trustworthy Raven correspondent on cross-continental matters; the other long-distance fliers (terns, gulls, certain swallows, certain less-famous corvids) are, by the Murder's own published commentary on bird testimony, considered narrators of varying reliability. Inkbeak's distinguishing characteristic, by Federación-side description, is that he is, "alone among visiting birds we have hosted, willing to acknowledge when he does not know a thing rather than continue to characterize the thing he does not know." The visiting-Raven roost at the Cartagena harbor wall — a tier of three perches, the middle being the senior perch — has been, by Federación standing protocol, in continuous service since Year 33; the wax on the middle perch is renewed by Federación protocol on the day after each Inkbeak departure. Inkbeak's father (also Slatequill Inkbeak; the Sr./Jr. designation distinguishes them in Pittsburgh records) flew the regional pre-League Allegheny basin route for thirty-one years before retiring in Year 14.</dd>

              <dt>The Snowball / The Snowball Break</dt>
              <dd>A pre-Wave-Doctrine pattern in continuous-mode (Crown / Capture-the-Pole / Tag) matches. Once a team gathered a numerical lead at the active scoring objective, the lead snowballed: opposing knights returning to the field one at a time on rolling timers walked into a numerically superior defensive line and were knocked back out before they could mount a coordinated re-engagement. The trailing team's individual-return knights walked into a wall. The wall held. The wall scored. The match was, by minute three, decided. The <em>Snowball Break</em> is the inverse — the moment, under the Wave Doctrine, when the trailing team's wave returns in formation and breaks the leading team's wall. The two have become a paired tactical concept across the League's coaching literature: the snowball is the failure mode the doctrine fixes, the break is the success mode the doctrine produces. Coach Reyes of CYT, asked which he prefers as a coaching concept, answered: <em>"I prefer the break. I am, however, a Coyote. We have always been the trailing team in these matches. We have always wanted the wall to break. The Polar Bears, who have been the wall, prefer the snowball, and that is fair, and we will fight them about it next bracket."</em></dd>

              <dt>The Southern Continent</dt>
              <dd>The continent south of the Yucatan extension, comprising (by the basin coordinating council's Year 35 letter to the Yucatan League outpost) twenty-three settled lizard-line communities, eleven alligator-line communities, fourteen serpentine-line communities, and an indeterminate number of tropical bird communities. The League has, in three rounds of formal correspondence, attempted to extend admission to southern teams. The basin coordinating council has, in three rounds of formal response, politely declined. Stated reasons: travel distance (the Continental Rail does not connect south of the Yucatan extension; funding for a southern connection is not, by either side, available); predator-prey unease (the League's existing rosters include several species lines that register as predators in southern jungle ecology, and the southern serpentine communities have indicated they would prefer not to share locker tunnels with Lynx); and climate adaptation (the Helena Glacier Rink would be, by the southern coordinator's own assessment, lethal to a basin lizard within forty minutes of arrival). The coordinating council has, in its third response, extended a standing invitation: the League is welcome to play exhibition matches at southern venues — Lima Highlands Pitch, Caracas Canopy Hall, Buenos Aires Wetlands — and the southern communities will host hospitably. The League has not, as of Year 36, exercised the invitation. The Foundation has retained the option for a future season's pre-season exhibition slate.</dd>

              <dt>Spawn-Camping</dt>
              <dd>(historical, deprecated since Year 35.) The practice of firing on the opposing spawn line from one's own spawn line at the moment of round commencement. Possible because the original Year 28 field dimensions assumed ranged weapons of the era had effective ranges shorter than the spawn-to-spawn distance. The development of the Railgun in Year 32 invalidated the assumption. Spawn-camping was, for several seasons thereafter, a legal but widely-criticized opening tactic. The Year 35 field-widening — which placed the spawn lines one thousand eighty units apart, two hundred and twenty units beyond the maximum effective range of any current ranged weapon — eliminated the tactic. Coaches now refer to it in past tense, with mild relief.</dd>

              <dt>The Stadium Wars</dt>
              <dd>The Year 34 inter-city dispute when Reno, Tampa, and Fresno tried to buy each other's home stadiums. Resolved by Commissioner Whiskerstone, who sat on every contested deed for one consecutive month. Established the permanent League rule that stadiums cannot be sold; this is why neutral venues exist.</dd>

              <dt>The Steward's Pocket</dt>
              <dd>Locker-room shorthand for the bizarre incident in the Year 33 vault rotation, when a steward repeatedly arrived at the vault with a sealed bag containing one fewer item than the bag had been sealed with. The phrase "steward's pocket" now describes any object that goes missing without rational explanation.</dd>

              <dt>The Sundip Memorial Wing</dt>
              <dd>The wing of the Owl Hall in Seattle dedicated to Sundip Hootington Jr., OWL Sniper, who tied Hester Quillstrike's 412-pace record at the Reno Open Court in Year 35 R8 and died in the same match when the Power Core he climbed to celebrate the shot overloaded. The Wing is, by Owl tradition, the only knight memorial in the League named for a knight who tied rather than broke a record. The Owl Hall's board justified the dedication, in the original ratification statement: <em>"The shot was the equal of Quillstrike's. The Power Core's overload was, by League technical analysis, the result of a latency the Caucus has since patched. The shot stands. The shot tied. The Owl who took it died at the moment of celebration. We will, in his Hall's wing, keep his rifle and the Power Core's casing — the shot's two halves — and we will, in our seasons going forward, remember what the shot took."</em> The wing is open to the public during all Owl Hall business hours. Visitors are asked, at the door, to remove their hats. The hats remain off, by Owl Hall steward record, an average of fifty-one seconds per visitor. The Hall does not measure this; the Hall has, in two seasons, only known the average because a single Brewer's Reach Reader columnist measured it for a column the Reader's senior columnist refused to publish.</dd>

            </dl>
          </details>

          <details class="lore-glossary-bucket" open>
            <summary><span class="bucket-letter">T</span> <span class="bucket-count">6 terms</span></summary>
            <dl class="lore-glossary-bucket-list">
              <dt>Tactical Erasure</dt>
              <dd>Sniper jargon, originating with the Tampa Sharks scouts' shared journal: a kill on a Healer that determines the outcome of an engagement before the engagement has even begun. Many Snipers find the term distasteful but most consider it accurate.</dd>

              <dt>Tactical Self-Sacrifice</dt>
              <dd>The League's official designation for the act of intentionally absorbing fatal damage to deny the kill or its effect to the opposing team. First codified after Old Bristlebeard the First ate a grenade in the inaugural championship final to deny it to the Wolves. Counts as a normal kill in the stats but is decorated separately in the Hall.</dd>

              <dt>The Third Clam</dt>
              <dd>The third of three small clams left by Crash Wartooth (WLF Brawler) at the Helena Glacier Rink concession-stand standing rail on the evening of the Year-32 R3 match between the Hedgehogs and the Wolves. The clams paid for two cups of hot tea bought side-by-side, in silence, by Wartooth and Avery Loambright (HED Healer). Wartooth left first and put three additional clams on the rail beside Loambright's empty cup. Loambright did not take them. At the next Year-32 HED-WLF match (R7), Wartooth and Loambright each silently took one clam. The third clam remained. After Loambright's death in the Year-33 final and after The Bow that followed it, no one — neither Wartooth, who outlived her, nor any subsequent venue steward, nor any subsequent Hedgehog or Wolf knight — has taken the third clam. The Helena venue has not, in the four seasons since, swept the rail. The clam is, as of the Year-36 mid-season Foundation audit, still on the rail. The rail is, by every Helena venue staff member's standing acknowledgment, "to be left as it is, on this matter, indefinitely." The Foundation Library catalogs the clam under the file name "Year-32-R3-rail.note." The note's body is six words: <em>"the third one is for them."</em> The note is unsigned.</dd>

              <dt>The Three Pressures</dt>
              <dd>Pell Whittlestone's Year-24 working theory of float-gas stability — the foundational technical paper she wrote at age twenty-one for an upper-Idaho regional engineering quarterly, on the strength of which the Boise Float Gas Foundry hired her four seasons before the founding bell. The paper proposed, against the then-prevailing single-pressure stability model, that float-gas operates under three distinct pressure regimes which transition at predictable thresholds, and that the dominant balloon-engineering practice of the time was optimizing for the wrong regime. Initially rejected by the regional engineering board for being "speculative beyond the available evidence." Within three years it was the Foundry's working standard. The board has, in two subsequent papers, retracted the rejection without naming Whittlestone; she has, in twenty years, declined to ask them to. <b>The colloquial second meaning:</b> Featherquill's Year-33 column on the Tinkerbarrel disclosure characterized Whittlestone's refusal to elaborate as "the second pressure." The phrase passed into League shorthand. Today, when a Caucus member declines to elaborate on a procedural matter, the standard recognition is "the second pressure." Whittlestone has not commented on the shorthand.</dd>

              <dt>The Tinkerbarrel Disclosure</dt>
              <dd>The serial publication, in <em>The Lobster Reach Daily</em> across Year 33's spring quarter, of retired Sharks equipment manager Reef Tinkerbarrel's career memoir, including the eighth installment which contained the full text of his Year 30 R3 equipment-manager logbook documenting the Sharks' undeclared use of a flat (under-pressure) Float Gas batch in their home shutout of the Foxes. The disclosure prompted the Year 33 Caucus working session at which the Year 30 R3 result was — over the Foxes' formal objection — allowed to stand, on Whittlestone's argument that the exploit was a Foundry-side delivery failure no team in Year 30 had the technical capability to remediate properly, and that the Foundry's Year-31 protocol upgrade had eliminated the exploit's feasibility. The disclosure also produced the eighth installment's most-read print run in the publication's twenty-three-year history — the print run had to be doubled mid-week. Tinkerbarrel did not, on disclosure, request payment from the publication beyond his standard memoir serialization rate. He has, by his post-retirement statement, no further memoirs in preparation.</dd>

              <dt>The Tokens of an Unknown Place</dt>
              <dd>Two small wooden tokens tendered as payment for one lobster at the Brewer's Reach Concession Row booth in Year 36 mid-season by a Quetzal who did not speak League Common. The tokens are of a kind not, by the lobster vendor's nine-season memory, previously seen at the booth. The Foundation Library, on the booth's permission, examined the tokens in Year 36 closeout and was unable to identify their origin: the wood is not local to any of the twenty League cities; the markings on the face are not in any of the three written languages currently active on the continent; the carving style does not match any known pre-Long-Quiet artifact in the Library's reference collection. The tokens are, by the lobster vendor's standing rule, not for sale and not for further review. They remain in the booth's lock-box, beneath the bowls of unground sea-salt. The Library has, on the vendor's request, not pressed the matter further. The Foundation Drawer's curator has filed a single line in the master index: <em>"see the lobster vendor's lock-box. the answer is, on this matter, hers to keep."</em></dd>

            </dl>
          </details>

          <details class="lore-glossary-bucket" open>
            <summary><span class="bucket-letter">V</span> <span class="bucket-count">2 terms</span></summary>
            <dl class="lore-glossary-bucket-list">
              <dt>The Vendor</dt>
              <dd>The lobster vendor on Concession Row at Brewer's Reach Pitch. Has been at her booth since before the inaugural match (Year 28) and has not, for any reason, ever moved her booth. Her prices have not changed since the League's founding — one bit per lobster, with the small wax cup of melted butter included. The Float Foundation's sole lobster supplier, by long-standing tradition. Refuses, on every Foundation request, to raise her prices to match the Foundation's official concession-stand pricing. The Foundation has, on three occasions, requested that she do so. She has, on three occasions, declined. The Foundation has, on three occasions, declined to close the booth. Her name is not, by long-standing personal preference, on any Foundation document. The Foundation refers to her, in formal correspondence, as <em>"the Vendor."</em> The Vendor is, by the Brewer's Reach Reader column <em>"On the Vendor Who Has Not Moved,"</em> the longest-serving institution in the entire Float Knights organization — older than the Commissioner, older than the LMG broadcast booth, older than Pell Whittlestone's Foundry, older than the founding match itself.</dd>

              <dt>The Vendor's Bell</dt>
              <dd>A small brass bell at the corner of the lobster vendor's booth at Brewer's Reach Pitch's Concession Row. The bell is rung by the vendor, by long-standing personal practice, when a child purchases their first lobster from her stall. The bell rings once. The vendor does not announce the ring. The vendor does not, by any accessible record, count the rings. The bell has been at the booth since the booth opened. The bell's clapper, by Foundation steward measurement, has worn approximately four millimeters of brass over eight seasons. The bell will, by reasonable extrapolation, last approximately three more lifetimes at this rate. The vendor has not, by any account, ever moved the bell from its corner. The bell rings, by booth steward's count, on average twice per match-day. The total ring count is, by no one's count, a knowable number. The bell rings. The child gets a piece of paper, in extraordinary circumstances. The child, in ordinary circumstances, gets a lobster, melted butter, and a moment in which a vendor sees them and rings a bell. This is enough.</dd>

            </dl>
          </details>

          <details class="lore-glossary-bucket" open>
            <summary><span class="bucket-letter">W</span> <span class="bucket-count">4 terms</span></summary>
            <dl class="lore-glossary-bucket-list">
              <dt>The Wave Doctrine</dt>
              <dd>League rule, ratified Year 36 founding bell. Governs respawn formation: when three or more knights of a single team have been downed in the same round, they respawn together at a single bench-side line, then walk together back onto the pitch as a connected wave during a seven-second formation period. The Doctrine includes a slowest-knight sprint allowance — the slowest knight in the wave is granted a temporary speed adjustment so the wave does not stretch out into a disorganized trickle on the way to the center engagement. In continuous-mode tournaments (Crown, Capture-the-Pole, Tag), the Doctrine applies on a fixed-delay timer rather than the round-based three-knight threshold. Designed by the Caucus to break the snowball — the previous staggered-respawn protocol's tendency to compound a team's losses by re-introducing downed knights piecemeal into a still-standing opposing line. The Doctrine produced two consecutive comeback wins in its first two sanctioned applications (RCC vs PLR Year 36 R2 Crown, and the second under the regular-match three-knight rule); Pell Whittlestone has called it <em>"the second-largest single-rule contribution to the League's tactical balance since the Marshmallow Protocol"</em> and is, by her own admission, "still not certain whether that ranking is too high or too low." The seven-second walk has, by Featherquill's column "On Watching the Wave," become an informally-protected window in which downed knights exchange brief teammate-to-teammate sentences before re-engagement; the Caucus's draft minutes proposing a four-second reduction were amended to retain the seven-second minimum after the column ran.</dd>

              <dt>Whitefang the Suspected</dt>
              <dd>A name appearing in graffiti throughout Brewer's Reach Pitch and (by sporadic report) at six other venues across the continent. Whitefang is not, by any League record, a knight. Whitefang is not, by any team record, a player. Whitefang's existence is unconfirmed. Whitefang's signature appears, by Foundation cleaner records, in three different handwritings across at least four seasons of bathroom-stall and locker-tunnel scribblings. The Foundation has, on six occasions, attempted to identify the writer (or writers); the Foundation has, on six occasions, given up. Whitefang is, by every honest reading, a running collaborative joke maintained by an unknown number of fans across multiple cities. The Foundation has stopped trying to clean the writings off completely. The Foundation now, by long-standing janitor preference, leaves the most-recent Whitefang scribble intact and only cleans the older ones. The result is that Brewer's Reach has, at any given moment, exactly one Whitefang scribble visible, somewhere in the building. The most recent (Year 36 R5) is in the third stall of the men's washroom in the upper concourse, in red gel-pen, and reads: <em>"WHITEFANG WAS NEVER HERE — and was here anyway"</em>.</dd>

              <dt>The Whittlestone Address</dt>
              <dd>The League's ceremonial founding-bell convocation speech, delivered at the start of every season the League adds a new team or changes its standing rule book. Originally drafted by Pell Whittlestone (then Foundation Counsel) for the Year-31 founding bell, when the Foxes joined; preserved in canonical form across every subsequent convocation by Whittlestone's successors and the Caucus chairs after her. Three numbered points: (1) the League is a tournament that is also a covenant; (2) every team brings something the League agreed to honor; (3) a League that does not honor what each team brought is "not a League. it is a competition." The middle passage enumerates each team in alphabetical-by-city order with one exactly-fourteen-words sentence describing their pre-League tradition; the count is preserved across the founding twelve plus the eight Continental Expansion teams (twenty fourteen-word sentences as of Year 36). The closing four lines, plus the canonical eleven-second pause between lines three and four, run exactly eleven seconds — the second of the League's two canonical eleven-second silences (the other being The Bow). The address is, by Caucus standing rule, the only public address required by the bylaws.</dd>

              <dt>The Wide Draw</dt>
              <dd>A Boise Brawling Badgers tactical pattern, drilled into the team's Year 36 training camp by head coach Brockholm Slatebrush. Functionally identical to the Coyotes' drift pattern (la borradura), but renamed by Slatebrush so the Badgers — who would not, by their own coaching staff's frank admission, willingly run a tactic called "the drift" — would adopt it. The Caucus's tactical archive has not, formally, recognized the equivalence. Slatebrush has not, formally, denied the equivalence. Featherquill, asked off the record, said: <em>"The Badgers are running the Coyote tactic and calling it something else. The Coyotes have noticed. The Coyotes are flattered. The Coyotes are also planning to drift around the wide draw, which is a thing only the Coyotes know how to do, and which will be, in the Badgers' R7 match against the Antlerlords, an interesting moment for both teams."</em></dd>

            </dl>
          </details>
        </dl>
      </article>
    </div>

<div class="tab-content" data-tab="about">
  <div class="about-page">
    <h2>ℹ️ About Float Knights</h2>
    <div class="sub">An auto-playing mascot tournament sim. Cute, cuddly <b>dodgeball but with guns</b> — that's the closest description. Cute animals in medieval armor wielding futuristic weapons. HP = balloons. Death is permanent (eventually).</div>

    <div class="credits">
      <div class="block">
        <h3>How it works</h3>
        <p><b>20 teams</b> in the league as of Year 36 mid-season (12 founders + 4 Year 35 closeout expansion teams: Tigers, Polar Bears, Bison, Ravens + 4 Year 36 mid-season Continental Expansion teams: Lynx, Moose, Coyotes, Quetzals). Each season randomly draws 12 teams into the qualifier-then-eight-team ladder — 4 qualifier matches → 4 quarterfinals → 2 semifinals → final. Bracket size is configurable down to 4 in Settings. Each match is best-of-5 rounds. Each round is a <b>7-on-7</b> elimination fight (Healers and Grenadiers joined the original five archetypes in v22).</p>
        <p>A round averages around 40-45 seconds. A full match runs 3-5 minutes. Bets are placed between rounds.</p>
        <p>Knights have <b>3 lives per match</b>. When KO'd in a round, they respawn the next round — <b>unless they've used all 3 lives</b>, in which case they die permanently and their gear drops on the field for survivors to scavenge. Scavenged gear keeps its previous owner's name and accumulates a lineage chain across the league's history.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="block">
        <h3>The seven archetypes</h3>
        <ul style="line-height:1.7;">
          <li><b>🛡️ Tank</b> — heavy plate, slow movement, soaks hits. Doesn't dodge.</li>
          <li><b>⚔️ Striker</b> — balanced offense, the tournament's workhorse class.</li>
          <li><b>💨 Speedster</b> — squishy, fast, the best dodger on the field.</li>
          <li><b>👊 Brawler</b> — close-quarters specialist with crit potential.</li>
          <li><b>🎯 Sniper</b> — long-range, glass cannon. Snipers preferentially target healers.</li>
          <li><b>✚ Healer</b> — support unit. Heals the lowest-HP teammate over time. Has a minimum range (won't melee), so it physically follows whoever it's healing. May wander across the battlefield when switching heal targets.</li>
          <li><b>💣 Grenadier</b> — throws ONE grenade at the start of an engagement, dealing AoE damage. Then falls back to weak melee — bring 'em early.</li>
        </ul>
      </div>

      <div class="block">
        <h3>What the AI actually does</h3>
        <ul style="line-height:1.7;">
          <li><b>Tactical formations</b> — six pre-positioning patterns (line, wedge, phalanx, echelon, killbox, flying-V) selected per team per round. Roles fill slots by tactical priority — tanks anchor the front (or center, in the killbox), healers trail safely, speedsters lead the flying-V's point. Different formations match up differently, so the opening of a round actually matters now.</li>
          <li>Shows mercy to low-HP enemies; flees on low HP toward health pickups</li>
          <li>Hunts down attackers (mercy state); swarms toward visible enemies</li>
          <li>Picks up and uses items, scavenges fallen gear if it's an upgrade</li>
          <li>Navigates around terrain blocks (corner-stuck strafe to round walls)</li>
          <li><b>Dodges incoming projectiles</b> — Speedsters dodge often, Snipers rarely, Tanks not at all. Per-knight cooldown so dodges punctuate, not dominate. Low-HP knights in melee can dodge BACKWARDS to disengage from scrums.</li>
          <li>Random crits and misses; weapon inaccuracy creates natural variance</li>
          <li>Snipers don't camp the corner anymore; they kite to ~50% of weapon range</li>
          <li>Pushes the center for the Power Core when a teammate is closest</li>
          <li>Knockback on every hit, scaled by damage and reduced by armor</li>
        </ul>
      </div>

      <div class="block">
        <h3>Match details</h3>
        <ul style="line-height:1.7;">
          <li>Player names are <b>massively</b> randomized (~4.1 billion combinations) — you won't see a duplicate twice in a lifetime</li>
          <li>Projectiles have physics: velocity, range, swept collision, pierce-prevention through walls</li>
          <li>Knights, terrain, and projectiles all collide; dropped items have hitboxes</li>
          <li>Field obstacle placement is randomized per match (Power Core gets a guaranteed clear zone in the center)</li>
          <li><b>1,920 stadium variations</b> — generated by a three-axis factory: 20 cities × 8 sports × 12 effect overlays (Stock + Foundry + Underdig + Submerged + Nightwoods + Hallowtide + Petalfall + Frostfall + Neonspark + Bramble + Aurora + Harvest). Each combination is visually distinct: a Phoenix Sandstone Foundry Pitch doesn't look like a Yukon Tundra-Silver Submerged Pitch. Stadium picked per match; full preview catalog browsable in the Lore tab with an effect-picker for the 12 variants.</li>
          <li>Match outcomes are <b>seeded and procedurally generated</b> — same seed reproduces the same match exactly, every time</li>
          <li>Sim speed is adjustable (bottom-right of the arena)</li>
          <li>The bottom <b>stock-ticker</b> rolls live scores, top streaks, lost-loot callouts, and recent feed events</li>

<!-- ============================================================
     SIMULATION — Part A
     Constants, name generator, position archetypes, league state
     ============================================================ -->
<script>
'use strict';

/* ============================================================
   RNG + MATH HELPERS
   All randomness used by the simulation routes through SIM_RNG, a
   seeded mulberry32 PRNG. Two clients running with the same seed
   produce byte-identical match outcomes — the foundation for shared
   live matches (see ROADMAP.md Tier 1).

   `Math.random()` is preserved for non-simulation purposes (UI
   nicety, visual jitter that doesn't affect outcome). The helpers
   below (R, RI, pick, pickN, shuffle) ALWAYS use the seeded RNG.
   ============================================================ */

// mulberry32 — fast, good distribution, period 2^32
function mulberry32(seed) {
  let s = seed >>> 0;
  return function() {
    s = (s + 0x6D2B79F5) >>> 0;
    let t = s;
    t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
    t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

// Hash a string to a uint32 (FNV-1a). Used for stable match seeds.
function hashStr(s) {
  let h = 2166136261 >>> 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    h ^= s.charCodeAt(i);
    h = Math.imul(h, 16777619);
  }
  return h >>> 0;
}

// Deterministic seed for a given (season, slot) pair. The genesis seed is
// stable per league (set once on initLeague + persisted), so two clients
// loading the same saved state derive the same match seed.
function computeMatchSeed(season, slot) {
  const genesis = (typeof LEAGUE !== "undefined" && LEAGUE.genesisSeed) || 0xF107C001;
  return hashStr(`${genesis}:s${season}:${slot}`);
}

// Global RNG state for the simulation. Seeded at match start (and
// inherited from saved league state for determinism across reloads).
const SIM_RNG = {
  seed: 0,
  next: () => Math.random(), // overwritten on first reseed
  reseed(seed) {
    this.seed = seed >>> 0;
    this.next = mulberry32(this.seed);
  },
};
// Separate RNG for visual-only biome/scatter generation. Reseeded at
// match start with a DIFFERENT transformation of the match seed so its
// stream is independent of the combat RNG. This guarantees that adding
// or removing a biome decoration call in the future never affects
// combat outcomes — visuals and gameplay use independent streams.
const BIOME_RNG = {
  seed: 0,
  next: () => Math.random(),
  reseed(seed) {
    // XOR with a separate constant so this stream diverges from SIM_RNG
    // even when both are seeded from the same match seed.
    this.seed = (seed ^ 0x9E3779B9) >>> 0;
    this.next = mulberry32(this.seed);
  },
};
// Initial seed — replaced as soon as the first match starts. Using a
// fixed integer here means a fresh league always boots identically
// until startMatch() reseeds with a per-match seed.
SIM_RNG.reseed(0xF107C001);
BIOME_RNG.reseed(0xF107C001);

function R(min, max) { return SIM_RNG.next() * (max - min) + min; }
function RI(min, max) { return Math.floor(R(min, max + 1)); }
function pick(arr) { return arr[Math.floor(SIM_RNG.next() * arr.length)]; }
function pickN(arr, n) {
  const c = arr.slice();
  const out = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n && c.length; i++) {
    out.push(c.splice(Math.floor(SIM_RNG.next() * c.length), 1)[0]);
  }
  return out;
}
function shuffle(arr) {
  const a = arr.slice();
  for (let i = a.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(SIM_RNG.next() * (i + 1));
    [a[i], a[j]] = [a[j], a[i]];
  }
  return a;
}
function clamp(v, lo, hi) { return Math.max(lo, Math.min(hi, v)); }
function distance(a, b) {
  const dx = a.x - b.x, dy = a.y - b.y;
  return Math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy);
}
/* === v37.21: Squared-distance helper for comparisons. ===
   Most "is target A closer than target B" checks don't need the
   actual distance — only the relative ordering, which is preserved
   by comparing squared distances. Skipping the sqrt is ~2-3× faster
   in tight inner loops (per-knight per-frame nearest-enemy scans).
   Use distSq() when you're comparing to another distance threshold
   (square the threshold once outside the loop) or to another distSq()
   result. Use distance() when you actually need the metric value. */
function distSq(a, b) {
  const dx = a.x - b.x, dy = a.y - b.y;
  return dx*dx + dy*dy;
}

/* ============================================================
   NAME GENERATOR
   Embedded from user's "simple random name generator" (4-syllable
   fantasy-style: Capital + lowercase + middle syllable + ending).
   Produces names like "Qarchlut", "Bearson", "Acackadain".

   To swap in a different generator:
     - Replace the four arrays below, OR
     - Replace genFirstName() to call your source.
   ============================================================ */
const NG_W1 = ["Q","A","B","C","D","E","F","G","H","I","J","K","L","M","N","O","P","R","S","T","U","V","W","X","Y","Z"];
const NG_W2 = ["a","c","e","f","h","l","m","n","o","r","s","t","u","x","y"];
const NG_W3 = ["rch","a","ack","ad","agg","ah","ai","al","an","ana","ar","ara","as","b","c","ch","ck","d","dwyn","e","ea","ear","ee","eira","ek","el","end","er","ex","ey","f","g","gn","h","i","iar","ig","il","ill","im","imma","in","in","inu","io","ion","ip","ir","iri","irm","irsa","is","ish","isil","ito","iz","izu","j","ka","ko","l","la","lar","lbor","le","le","les","ll","lm","ln","ls","m","me","mm","mo","n","na","nd","ne","nk","nt","nt","ntin","o","ock","og","om","on","oo","ory","our","p","ph","r","ra","rc","re","ren","ri","rn","ro","rr","rra","rv","s","se","sh","sh","sl","so","t","ta","te","tz","u","ull","us","us","ve","x","y","ynn","yo","zer"];
const NG_W4 = ["lut","aam","adain","adon","ain","aira","ais","ako","alary","ald","aliam","aline","ama","amari","ami","an","anan","ander","ankem","ano","aot","ar","ari","aroch","aron","ary","as","asha","asia","ay","azan","bbert","brone","cinbe","ck","cko","dai","dain","dalis","ddery","den","dian","dor","eah","eal","eam","ean","edain","ee","een","eif","enain","enar","enard","endon","eous","era","erm","eron","ery","ery","ethel","eve","even","eybol","fer","fir","firem","frey","gal","garom","gawa","gen","ggy","gil","gin","gon","gout","ham","haru","haun","helle","heo","hera","hina","hon","ht","iador","iam","ian","ias","iba","ice","igan","iko","ill","ilus","imor","ine","inus","ion","ira","is","ita","ka","katt","ker","ket","key","ku","la","lain","lash","ld","le","lem","ley","liaf","ll","lliden","loki","ma","main","mar","mara","maros","mer","mi","mie","mon","mor","morn","ndus","ndy","nell","ner","net","nny","nor","ntz","nuary","oconi","odenn","odor","off","old","om","omi","omoru","onton","onus","oole","oot","oot","oram","orm","orn","ory","ouhm","oum","ouos","ous","pher","pike","ra","rah","ran","rd","rea","ree","rem","ren","ri","rio","rlie","rom","ron","ros","rot","rry","run","rynn","shima","shin","son","sose","ta","tac","tain","tall","tar","ter","terian","thain","thor","thorne","tide","to","tone","tor","uce","udain","uib","ull","us","use","use","va","vid","von","wran","wrath","xander","xia","xieam","xoust","yle","zell","zuo"];

function genFirstName() {
  return pick(NG_W1) + pick(NG_W2) + pick(NG_W3) + pick(NG_W4);
}

/* Mascot surnames — give the fantasy first name a sports-flavored last name */
const SURNAMES = [
  "Whiskers","Pawington","Snouter","Furr","Nibbles","Talons","Scales","Thunderclaw",
  "Finsworth","Tailwhip","Brushfoot","Glimmerfang","Hootington","Bubblesnap","Dustfeather",
  "Bristle","Mossback","Quillbeard","Velvetfoot","Pebble","Ironclaw","Dapplecoat",
  "Wartooth","Fizzlepaw","Marshmallow","Pricklesnoot","Chompers","Whisper",
  "Hopstride","Dribblepaw","Snufflenose","Crashfoot"
];
const SUFFIXES = ["", "", "", "", "", "II", "III", "Jr.", "the Bold", "the Ferocious", "the Cute"];

function genFullName() {
  let parts = [genFirstName(), pick(SURNAMES)];
  const sx = pick(SUFFIXES);
  if (sx) parts.push(sx);
  return parts.join(" ");
}

const LEAGUE_CONFIG = {
  bracketSize: 12, // 4 / 8 / 12 (12 = qualifier round → 8-team ladder). v28.13: bumped to 12 for the 20-team continental expansion — 12 of 20 teams play each season, and the qualifier-round format gives top-ranked teams byes for narrative interest
  // Visual / accessibility toggles. All default to false (effects ON).
  // The render layer reads these per-frame so toggling takes immediate effect.
  disableShake: false,
  // v37.14: disableFieldFx removed — split into granular flags
  // (disableCloudShadows, disableAmbientParticles, disableSlowMo).
  // Legacy users with disableFieldFx:true are migrated at boot; see the
  // toggle wiring code in bindSettings.
  // v37.10: disableLighting removed — split into granular flags below.
  // Legacy users with disableLighting:true are migrated at boot; see the
  // toggle wiring code in bindSettings.
  disableVignette: false,    // sky-tint vignette (was under disableLighting umbrella)
  disablePitchLights: false, // corner pitch lights (was under disableLighting umbrella)
  disableDropShadows: false, // player drop shadows (was under disableLighting umbrella)
  disableSlowMo: false,      // slow-motion on match-deciding KO (was under disableFieldFx umbrella)
  disableCrowd: false,     // stadium spectators border + cheer-on-KO
  highFrameRate: false,    // false = 30fps cap (default, smooth on most devices)
                           // true  = 60fps cap (matches device refresh, smoother
                           //         but doubles render work). Sim tick rate is
                           //         independent (20fps) so this only changes
                           //         draw frequency, not gameplay speed.
  // === v28 game mode selector + per-mode config ===
  // gameMode determines how a match is structured. "deathmatch" is the
  // canonical 5v5 best-of-N round-elimination mode. The three new modes
  // run as a single continuous "match" with different scoring rules.
  gameMode: "deathmatch",  // "deathmatch" | "koth" | "ctf" | "tag"
  modeConfig: {
    koth: {
      pointsToWin: 50,    // 25 / 50 / 100 supported
      tickPointsPerSec: 1, // points per second for crown holder
    },
    ctf: {
      capsToWin: 5,       // 3 / 5 / 7 / 9
      teamSize: 7,        // bots per team in CTF (request: "teams of 7")
      flagReturnSec: 8,   // seconds before dropped flag returns to center
      carrierSpeedMult: 0.80,
    },
    tag: {
      // "Damage scaled high enough that rounds take under 90 seconds"
      // It stays It, target freezes 3s then unfreezes (per spec). Damage
      // applied: per-hit (small chunk) + bleed during 3s freeze (heavy).
      // Total per-tag = tagDamagePerHit + tagDpsWhileFrozen × 3 sec.
      // With 50 + (130 × 3) = 440 damage, average bots die in 1-2 tags.
      tagFreezeFrames: 60,    // 3 seconds @ 20fps
      tagDamagePerHit: 50,    // immediate damage on tag
      tagDpsWhileFrozen: 130, // bleed dps during 3-second freeze
    },
  },
};

/* ============================================================
   MATCH STRUCTURE — best-of-N rounds + lives per match
   Each "match" in the bracket (semifinal, final) is best-of-5
   rounds. Each round is a 5v5 elimination fight. Knights have
   3 lives per match — a round-loss costs them one. Run out of
   lives and they die permanently, dropping their gear.
   ============================================================ */
const MATCH = {
  bestOf: 5,           // number of rounds total
  roundsToWin: 3,      // first-to-N (must be ceil(bestOf/2))
  startingLives: 3,    // each player gets this many lives per match
  interRoundDelay: 0,  // milliseconds (0 = pause for user input)
};

/* ============================================================
   EQUIPMENT — weapons, armor, items
   Each player carries a loadout {weapon, armor, item}. When they
   die, the loadout drops at their corpse and surviving players
   may scavenge it. Picked-up gear is renamed
     "<owner>'s <gear name> (scavenged)"
   and persists with that name (cascading if scavenged again).
   ============================================================ */

/* Melee fallback profiles — used by AI's MELEE state when a ranged-weapon
   bot is being swarmed. We don't actually swap inventories (that would
   confuse the scavenging system); we just use one of these profiles for
   the resolveAttack call when the bot is in MELEE state.
   pickMeleeFallback() runs at match start, deterministic via SIM_RNG so
   reseeded matches reproduce exactly. */
const MELEE_FALLBACKS = [
  { id: "_fb_punch",  ico: "👊", name: "Bare Knuckles",   dmgMod: -2, defMod: 0, cdMod: -0.10, critMod: 0,     stun: 0,    range: 18, projSpeed: 0, inacc: 0 },
  { id: "_fb_dagger", ico: "🗡", name: "Belt Dagger",     dmgMod:  0, defMod: 0, cdMod: -0.05, critMod: +0.04, stun: 0,    range: 20, projSpeed: 0, inacc: 0 },
  { id: "_fb_kick",   ico: "🦵", name: "Boot Kick",       dmgMod: -1, defMod: 0, cdMod:  0,    critMod: 0,     stun: 0.05, range: 18, projSpeed: 0, inacc: 0 },
];
function pickMeleeFallback(p) {
  // Deterministic per (matchSeed, player.id). We use a hash so changing
  // player order doesn't reshuffle assignments.
  const h = ((p.id || 0) * 2654435761) >>> 0;
  return MELEE_FALLBACKS[h % MELEE_FALLBACKS.length];
}

// "Score" a piece of gear so the AI can compare its current piece to
// a scavengable upgrade. Higher = better for that slot.
// Crucially, this is now POSITIONAL — a Sniper values a Railgun more than
// a stronger-on-paper weapon they don't know how to use, so we don't get
// every survivor swapping to the absolute strongest piece.
function gearScore(slot, gear, ownerPosition) {
  if (!gear) return 0;
  if (slot === "weapon") {
    let s = gear.dmgMod * 2.5 + gear.defMod * 1.2 + (-gear.cdMod) * 6 + gear.critMod * 80 + gear.stun * 25;
    if (ownerPosition && gear.flavorPos === ownerPosition) s += 5;
    if (ownerPosition === "sniper" && gear.range > 200) s += 4;
    if (ownerPosition === "speed"  && gear.range > 100) s += 2;
    if ((ownerPosition === "tank" || ownerPosition === "brawl") && gear.range < 50) s += 3;
    return s;
  } else if (slot === "armor") {
    // Armor is now MORE valuable — defMod weighted 2.5x (was 1.5), spdMod 8x.
    // This is paired with the new defDenom=35 making each point of def
    // meaningfully reduce damage, so the AI's preference reflects actual impact.
    let s = gear.defMod * 2.5 + gear.spdMod * 8 + gear.critMod * 80;
    if (ownerPosition && gear.flavorPos === ownerPosition) s += 5;
    // Position-specific armor preferences
    if (ownerPosition === "tank" && gear.defMod >= 8) s += 4;   // tanks LOVE heavy armor
    if (ownerPosition === "speed" && gear.spdMod > 0) s += 4;   // speedsters love mobility
    if (ownerPosition === "sniper" && gear.critMod > 0) s += 3; // snipers love crit boost
    return s;
  } else if (slot === "item") {
    return 5;
  }
  return 0;
}

// Equip gear on a player and stamp the scavenged name if applicable.
// `gear` is a clone of a base WEAPON/ARMOR/ITEM definition with optional
// `displayName` and `originalOwner` fields when scavenged.
function gearDisplayName(gear) {
  if (!gear) return "";
  return gear.displayName || gear.name;
}

/* ============================================================
   PLAYER FACTORY (updated)
   Each new player spawns with a loadout matching their position by
   default — Tanks get Riot Shields & Plate Cuirass, Snipers get
   Railguns & Stealth Cloaks, etc. Items are randomized for variety.
   ============================================================ */
let _idCounter = 1;

function rollBaseStats() {
  return {
    hp:  RI(140, 200),  // was 70-120 — doubled for ~45s rounds
    dmg: RI(8, 22),
    def: RI(8, 30),     // was 5-25 — slightly higher floor
    spd: +(R(1.4, 2.6).toFixed(2)),
  };
}

function makePlayer(teamId, position) {
  const base = rollBaseStats();
  const bias = position.bias;
  const stats = {
    hp:  clamp(base.hp + bias.hp, 30, CAPS.hp),
    dmg: clamp(base.dmg + bias.dmg, 4, CAPS.dmg),
    def: clamp(base.def + bias.def, 0, CAPS.def),
    spd: clamp(+(base.spd + bias.spd).toFixed(2), 0.6, CAPS.spd),
    crit: clamp(COMBAT.baseCrit + bias.crit, 0.02, 0.30),
  };
  // Default loadout by position (with a fresh cloned object so scavenged
  // copies can be renamed without mutating the catalog).
  const defaultWeapon = WEAPONS.find(w => w.flavorPos === position.id) || WEAPONS[0];
  const defaultArmor  = ARMORS.find(a => a.flavorPos === position.id)  || ARMORS[0];
  const randomItem    = pick(ITEMS);
  return {
    id: _idCounter++,
    name: genFullName(),
    teamId,
    position: position.id,
    stats,
    // Loadout — start with default gear for the position
    weapon: { ...defaultWeapon },
    armor:  { ...defaultArmor },
    item:   { ...randomItem },
    // Career stats (persist across matches/seasons)
    career: { kills: 0, deaths: 0, matchesPlayed: 0, matchesWon: 0, seasonsPlayed: 0, scavenged: 0, longestStreak: 0, currentStreak: 0 },
    // === v37.23: Personality (career-persistent AI weighting) ===
    personality: pick(PERSONALITIES).id,
    // === v37.23: Rookie scouting report (generated lazily on profile open) ===
    scoutingReport: null,  // null until first opened; built by _generateScoutingReport
    // === v37.23: Injury status ===
    // null = healthy. When set: { type, matchesRemaining, statPenalty }
    injury: null,
    // Mortality
    deceased: false,
    deceasedSeason: null,
    deceasedBy: null,
    debutSeason: 1,
    // Match-time fields (reset per match)
    x: 0, y: 0, vx: 0, vy: 0,
    hp: stats.hp,
    alive: true,
    lives: MATCH.startingLives, // per-match lives (resets at match start)
    target: null,
    stunned: 0,        // frames remaining stunned (skip attacks)
    itemUsed: false,   // whether the consumable has fired this match
    boostMods: null,   // {dmg, spd, life} active boost from item
  };
}



// === v37.23: Knight injuries ===
// Sub-permadeath consequence. After a match, surviving knights have a
// chance to pick up an injury that holds them out 1-2 matches with a
// stat penalty on return. The penalty reflects in the eligible-roster
// check (startMatch / startRound) and the injured knight's lookups.
//
// Probability is gentle: 4% baseline, +6% if took a near-fatal hit
// (final-life KO this match), +2% per round played past 5. Caps at 14%.
// Roughly one injury every 3-4 matches at normal play, more after grueling
// 7-round affairs.
const INJURIES = [
  { type: "wrenched_shoulder", label: "Wrenched shoulder", desc: "The shoulder went on a stun absorption.", missMatches: 1, penalty: { dmg: 0.85 } },
  { type: "ankle_strain",      label: "Ankle strain",      desc: "Came down wrong on a corner cut.",      missMatches: 1, penalty: { spd: 0.85 } },
  { type: "concussion",        label: "Concussion",        desc: "Took a helmet-rattle off a Plasma Mace.", missMatches: 2, penalty: { dmg: 0.90, def: 0.85 } },
  { type: "rib_bruise",        label: "Bruised ribs",      desc: "Soaked too many rounds at point-blank.", missMatches: 1, penalty: { hp: 0.90 } },
  { type: "draw_arm_strain",   label: "Drawing-arm strain",desc: "The Sniper's archery shoulder.",         missMatches: 2, penalty: { dmg: 0.85 } },
  { type: "burnout",           label: "Burnout",           desc: "Five-round match. Exhausted.",            missMatches: 1, penalty: { spd: 0.92, dmg: 0.92 } },
];

/* Roll an injury for a survivor at match end. Mutates the player. */
function _rollPostMatchInjury(p, m) {
  if (!p || p.deceased) return;
  if (p.injury) return; // already injured, don't double-up
  // Probability calc
  let prob = 0.04;
  if (p.lives === 1) prob += 0.06; // came within one balloon of dying
  const roundsPlayed = m && m.currentRoundIndex ? m.currentRoundIndex : 0;
  if (roundsPlayed > 5) prob += (roundsPlayed - 5) * 0.02;
  prob = Math.min(prob, 0.14);
  if (SIM_RNG.next() > prob) return;
  const inj = pick(INJURIES);
  p.injury = {
    type: inj.type,
    label: inj.label,
    desc: inj.desc,
    matchesRemaining: inj.missMatches,
    penalty: { ...inj.penalty },
  };
  feed("season", `🩹 ${TEAM_BY_ID[p.teamId]?.short || "?"}: ${escapeHTML(p.name)} sidelined with ${inj.label.toLowerCase()} (${inj.missMatches} match${inj.missMatches === 1 ? "" : "es"}).`);
}
window._rollPostMatchInjury = _rollPostMatchInjury;

/* Decrement injury counters at the START of a match for knights NOT
   selected (they sat out). When matchesRemaining hits 0, clear the
   injury. Called from startMatch. */
function _processInjuryStatuses(teamId) {
  const roster = LEAGUE.rosters[teamId];
  if (!roster) return;
  for (const p of roster) {
    if (!p || !p.injury) continue;
    p.injury.matchesRemaining--;
    if (p.injury.matchesRemaining <= 0) {
      const inj = p.injury;
      p.injury = null;
      feed("season", `🆗 ${TEAM_BY_ID[teamId]?.short || "?"}: ${escapeHTML(p.name)} returns from ${inj.label.toLowerCase()}.`);
    }
  }
}
window._processInjuryStatuses = _processInjuryStatuses;

// Lookup helper used by the post-match press conference and the
// team panel coach-row.

/* ============================================================
   RIVALRY HELPERS — v37.23
   Aggregate rivalry data for UI surfacing.
   ============================================================ */
function getRivalriesFor(knightId) {
  // Returns array of {otherId, theyKilledMe, iKilledThem, mutualSince}
  // for every other knight this one has interacted with (kills either way).
  if (!LEAGUE.rivalries || typeof knightId !== "number") return [];
  const seen = new Map();
  for (const key of Object.keys(LEAGUE.rivalries)) {
    const [aStr, bStr] = key.split("::");
    const a = parseInt(aStr, 10), b = parseInt(bStr, 10);
    if (a === knightId) {
      if (!seen.has(b)) seen.set(b, { otherId: b, iKilledThem: 0, theyKilledMe: 0 });
      seen.get(b).iKilledThem += LEAGUE.rivalries[key];
    } else if (b === knightId) {
      if (!seen.has(a)) seen.set(a, { otherId: a, iKilledThem: 0, theyKilledMe: 0 });
      seen.get(a).theyKilledMe += LEAGUE.rivalries[key];
    }
  }
  // Mark mutual rivals (both directions >= 3)
  const out = Array.from(seen.values());
  for (const r of out) r.isMutual = r.iKilledThem >= 3 && r.theyKilledMe >= 3;
  return out;
}
window.getRivalriesFor = getRivalriesFor;

/* Pre-match check: are any mutual rivalries on the field? Returns
   array of { aKnight, bKnight, aKilledB, bKilledA } for each mutual
   rival pair detected, or empty array if none. */
function detectActiveRivalries(m) {
  if (!m || !LEAGUE.rivalries) return [];
  const all = (m.teamAplayers || []).concat(m.teamBplayers || []);
  const onFieldIds = new Set(all.filter(p => !p.deceased).map(p => p.id));
  const pairs = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const key of Object.keys(LEAGUE.rivalries)) {
    const [aStr, bStr] = key.split("::");
    const a = parseInt(aStr, 10), b = parseInt(bStr, 10);
    if (!onFieldIds.has(a) || !onFieldIds.has(b)) continue;
    // Different teams only
    const ka = all.find(p => p.id === a);
    const kb = all.find(p => p.id === b);
    if (!ka || !kb || ka.teamId === kb.teamId) continue;
    const dedup = a < b ? a + "::" + b : b + "::" + a;
    if (seen.has(dedup)) continue;
    const fwd = LEAGUE.rivalries[a + "::" + b] || 0;
    const rev = LEAGUE.rivalries[b + "::" + a] || 0;
    if (fwd >= 3 && rev >= 3) {
      pairs.push({ aKnight: ka, bKnight: kb, aKilledB: fwd, bKilledA: rev });
      seen.add(dedup);
    }
  }
  return pairs;
}
window.detectActiveRivalries = detectActiveRivalries;

/* ============================================================
   SCOUTING REPORTS — v37.23
   One-line characterization of a rookie or veteran knight, generated
   at first profile-open and cached on the player. Templates draw on
   stat outliers + archetype + personality to produce evocative copy.
   ============================================================ */
function _generateScoutingReport(p) {
  if (!p) return "—";
  const pos = POS_BY_ID[p.position];
  const personality = PERSONALITY_BY_ID[p.personality] || PERSONALITY_BY_ID.methodical;
  const s = p.stats || {};
  const tier = (val, low, mid, high) => val >= high ? "high" : val >= mid ? "mid" : val >= low ? "low" : "vlow";

  // Stat outliers
  const hpTier = tier(s.hp,   100, 130, 165);
  const dmgTier = tier(s.dmg, 6,   10,  14);
  const spdTier = tier(s.spd, 1.0, 1.4, 1.8);
  const critTier = tier(s.crit, 0.05, 0.10, 0.18);

  const outliers = [];
  if (hpTier === "high")  outliers.push("walks heavy");
  if (hpTier === "vlow") outliers.push("brittle frame");
  if (dmgTier === "high") outliers.push("hits like a hammer-strike");
  if (dmgTier === "vlow") outliers.push("light hands, depends on positioning");
  if (spdTier === "high") outliers.push("moves fast enough to be hard to track");
  if (spdTier === "vlow") outliers.push("slow on the rotation");
  if (critTier === "high") outliers.push("a finisher's edge on the crit");
  if (critTier === "vlow") outliers.push("steady but rarely lucky");

  // Personality-driven framing line
  const personLines = {
    aggressive: ["closes harder than the position usually asks", "doesn't wait for the opening, makes one"],
    cautious:   ["picks her shots", "won't engage the wounded until the rest of the line is sorted"],
    showboat:   ["plays to the broadcast", "celebrates before he should"],
    loyal:      ["watches her healer like she's family", "the kind who stays with a downed teammate when the stunlock comes"],
    methodical: ["plays the percentages", "no surprises, no flair, just the math"],
  };
  const personLine = pick(personLines[personality.id] || personLines.methodical);

  // Archetype expectation lines
  const posExpect = {
    tank:      "expected to soak; the body will, in due course, tell us",
    striker:   "the position is the kill. she will, by every report, take the kill",
    speedster: "fast hands. faster feet. the league will, in due course, learn the rotation",
    brawler:   "close work. the close work will, by my read, pay",
    sniper:    "long shots. long waits. the work is, on the matter, the patience",
    healer:    "the line will, in due course, depend on her. she will, by every read, hold",
    grenadier: "we will, on this matter, watch the splash radius",
  };
  const posLine = posExpect[pos.id] || "the position is the position";

  let outlierClause = "";
  if (outliers.length === 1) outlierClause = ` — ${outliers[0]}`;
  else if (outliers.length >= 2) outlierClause = ` — ${outliers[0]}, ${outliers[1]}`;

  const verdict = pick([
    "watch the rotation",
    "by my read, ready",
    "the body will, in due course, tell us",
    "we are, on the matter, optimistic",
    "the cohort is, by my read, glad to have her",
    "promising",
    "the position will, in due course, be safe in these hands",
    "i will, on the matter, withhold further opinion until R3",
  ]);

  return `${pos.label.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + pos.label.slice(1)} rookie${outlierClause}. ${personLine.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + personLine.slice(1)}; ${posLine}. <em>${verdict}.</em>`;
}
window._generateScoutingReport = _generateScoutingReport;

/* Lazy accessor — generates if not yet cached, returns the string. */
function getScoutingReport(p) {
  if (!p) return "";
  if (!p.scoutingReport) {
    p.scoutingReport = _generateScoutingReport(p);
  }
  return p.scoutingReport;
}
window.getScoutingReport = getScoutingReport;
